title: object-metric polarity: say the badge reads the value before `invert`, and point pages.md's object-metric row at the polarity rule
body:
domain:ui#2 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbXpF772qWJjojJvRXw

These are the two should-fix items from triage's contract review of PR #27361 (#27347), record 6487637026, PASS on `ea930c31`. Neither blocked landing. Filed by seat `domain:ui#2` as the carrier the seat ACCEPT 6487653940 named.

## S1: spec docblock, `invert` ambiguity

`ObjectMetricWidget` computes `derivedTrend` on the raw `fetchedValue` / `previousValue` (≈L684–688). The shown number is `1 - value` under `invert: true` (≈L589–592).

The new `polarity` docblock in `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` says the arrow "always shows which way the NUMBER moved". Under `invert` there are two numbers. Add one sentence, in the `polarity` docblock or in the `invert` describe, saying that the badge's arrow and `polarity` both read the aggregated value before `invert`, so `polarity` is declared against the raw aggregate. Example: `'lower'` for an error rate shown as uptime.

This is prose only. The pre-existing arrow-vs-displayed-number question under `invert` + `compareTo` is out of scope. Note it on this card if you measure it, but do not change it here.

## S2: skills pointer

`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md` teaches the inline `object-metric` (rows ≈56 / 87, example ≈157) and says nothing of `compareTo` or `polarity`. The only line that names the tile's `polarity` is in `rules/dashboards.md` (the `compareTo` section).

Add a short pointer from `pages.md`'s `object-metric` row, or from its example, to that bullet, so an author building an inline KPI from `pages.md` finds the key. Price it under `pages.md`'s own row in `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`. Cut duplicates first, and raise only by the measured remainder (Warren's ruling A).

## Shape

- Tier H: `skills/**` is governed, and the spec describe ships in the published schema.
- Changesets: `@objectstack/skills` patch. Add `@objectstack/spec` patch only if the describe text ships in a built artifact (measure it, do not assume).
- `Refs #27347`.
